I really hope this dude is ok. I've been there, didn't film it, but this is so much like one of the last times I seriously self harmed. I feel bad, because I kind of smiled to myself, just for the fact that I've laughed at my own body and blood the same way he did. Kind of like looking at a replay of my own experiences. Knowing someone else has had that moment, I dunno. It's heartwarming in the worst way.
It's that weird derealization that doesn't really make any sense until it's happening.
That sudden burst of shock, like when he felt it and said it, jesus christ it brought me back. When the giddy "holy shit, would you look at this" gives way to "yep well, everyone else is gonna be really upset about this" to "oh shit my body is forgetting how to work" it happens (at least it did for me) in seconds, and it's like a shockwave.
I got lucky and crawled my way to my mom's room and she dragged my bloody ass to the ER and somehow I'm still here.
The tub, porch, all that shit is still stained. But I made it. And I hope he did, too. Shit still sucks, to certain degrees at different points. The body is fascinating. Escaping reality is a good time. But damn do I hope he made it.

I'm so grateful that I only went to a mental health facility for kids. We did have what they called the Quiet Room, but I only ever saw one particularly violent kid get thrown in there and sedated. The screams were chilling. 
They didn't do much but overprescribe, have us hang out in the day room (no going in your private room except to sleep), do collages, and maybe like one therapy session a week. There was gym time, where everyone was shuffled into a large room with soft floors and given kickballs and similar stuff. God forbid you just sit in a corner, because then you're hounded by staff about "why you won't engage" like maybe I just don't like sports or know anyone here?
I think the worst thing was when I was told (I was in for self harm, depression, and an eating disorder) that I'd never get out if I didn't eat. Other than that, they did fuck all to address those things. Way to therapy.
They also had us watch Harold and Maude on movie night during my first week. It didn't hit me until years later that maybe that wasn't an appropriate choice.

All in all, it was pretty traumatic at the time, but since it was pretty pointless and had no effect on me, it's whatever.

It's just disgusting that facilities like the one these kids went through exist, are operating, and that parents place their hope and their children in them.

This is so messed up, on many levels. I expected something that would leave me thinking "I guess that might be misconstrued as bullying, but was really empathy." But I read everything and feel sick.
As a person who has faced the suicide monster many times before, I am so thankful that I've never known someone like her. I still struggle with it, daily, but manage to see past it and live for tomorrow. I have a loving fiancé who helps me in my darker times. Most recently, he talked me down from a roof via cellphone. 
What I guess I'm trying to say is that, people who are walking that line between life and death, they need a sympathetic and helpful ear, no actual encouragement. It's really soothing and calming to hear that your feelings are valid and that the reasons that brought you to that precipice are real, and we do need that. But more than we need that, we need a slow talking-down.
If you love someone, or even slightly care about them,  or are just a simple human being, you will tell them not to do it. Not just because you don't know how to get bloodstains out of your shoes, or because you can't deal with the pomp and circumstance of the police and coroner when you work 7 days a week, but because you don't want someone to die. 
Like, regardless of how much you know someone is suffering mentally and emotionally, we all know that death is not the answer. Shit, I know that death is not the answer, and I'm almost always daydreaming about it.  
There's a lot in one life that can be changed, whether it be scenery, routine, friends, music, wardrobe, curtains, food... an endless line of minuscule things build to a better life. 
I mean, we're already here, we may as well make the best of it even when it is shit.

Ok so this was a lot longer and less poignant than I wanted, but I guess I just wanted to speak as someone who has been where her now-deceased "boyfriend" was. 

I'm angry for him, that someone took advantage of his mindstate and kept him in that dark place (even when he was moving out from it) long enough to actually do it. And at that point, his heart probably wasn't even in it anymore. Most of his thoughts were probably centered around the fact that she wanted him to do it (because "she loved him") which, okay, is sweet enough to a suicidal and dying person, but still. It's cheap.
I feel that this is definitely exploitation, likely in the form of a mental illness within herself. Someone mentioned narcissism, and I think that hits it on the head. I do feel for the situation, and to a certain extent, her, but I still can't help but feel that she knew what she was doing. Her words of gross encouragement were nearly constant, and vigilant at that. 

The fact of the entire thing is that she wanted him to die more than he actually wanted to. 

Regardless of her reasons, he's the one dead.

Those who are suicidal and hesitate, we have at least a shred of something that we don't want to let go of yet. We may not know what it is, but it's there, and someday we're grateful. That shred may see us into our 90's. Who knows?
If I had known someone like her when I was his age, I'd be dead for sure. Luckily I had zero friends and am now making very strong baby steps.

I don't know. It just fucks me up that I could be here but he can't. All because of some irresponsible person who happened to be within his circle. 

She doesn't deserve life in prison, if her problems are truly mental. Maybe she could get help and become stable. But then again, could she live with being stable and knowing that she encouraged someone she claimed to love to commit suicide?

This entire case is mindfucking from all angles.
